rationale: linpack-pc is a small (14 functions, ~19KB text) floating-point kernel benchmark whose execution time is dominated by tight loops in daxpy, dmxpy, dgefa, and dgesl, so the weight table favors low-overhead diversification over heavy control-flow transformation: SUB gets strong DiversityGain with moderate CorrectnessRisk because algebraic substitutions are cheap statically but can alter FP semantics, SPLIT is weighted as a near-free diversity booster for the larger functions (dmxpy, main), and IBR is kept at moderate RuntimeCost since indirect branching obscures loop structure but adds per-iteration dispatch overhead in the hot kernels. BCF and FLA carry high RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights so the selector applies them sparingly (e.g., only to cold setup code in main) rather than to the inner loops, where bogus predicates and dispatcher overhead would severely inflate benchmark runtime. ICALL is moderately favored given the program's few call sites and cheap indirection, while IGV is down-weighted on RuntimeCost because linpack's arrays are accessed with stride-critical inner loops where indirect global addressing costs measurable throughput; all CorrectnessRisk weights keep FP-safe transformation as a hard constraint.
